だるまそば.name: Daruma Soba
だるまそば.desc: A locally popular shop in Yamazato, Okinawa City. The signature dish is the Daruma soba with everything on top: bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), pig's feet (tebichi), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), in a gentle bonito broth soup. The specialty “bone soup” is popular too, and it fills up at lunchtime.
t: I ate here in November 2022.
Daruma Soba
You buy with meal tickets, and I ordered the “Daruma soba,” which shares the shop's name and is sold as “meal ticket No. 1” 😊
Daruma soba　¥900

The soup has the gentle taste of bonito broth 😊　The toppings are everything: bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), pig's feet (tebichi), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) 🤤　The noodles are medium-thick and there's plenty of volume too 😆
Rating (9/15): Just plain delicious. It's loved by local customers, and at lunchtime it fills up with customers. Daruma Soba's “bone soup” is delicious too, so please give it a try once.

上間沖縄天ぷら店.name: Uema Okinawa Tempura-ten
上間沖縄天ぷら店.desc: A shop with a long display of tempura, a “tempura shop where you can also eat soba.” The Uema way is to top the soupy ¥590 braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba with fish tempura and sausage tempura. The free tempura bits are a nice touch too, a shop rooted in the local community.
t: *This article was created with “Chat gpt 5.2 (Thinking)” and partially edited by me. I went to eat here in February 2025 😄

On my Okinawa soba tour, this time I went to “Uema Okinawa Tempura-ten” in Minami-Tōbaru, Okinawa City~ 😊　As the name says, the “tempura-first” vibe is already coming out from outside, and there are banners up too, so it's a perfect landmark. There were a lot of customers coming and going, and even before going in I felt, “Ah, this is the kind of place rooted in the local community” 🍤
Uema Okinawa Tempura-ten
Inside the shop
There's even a menu of Okinawan memorial service dishes 😆
Inside the shop

When you enter the shop, the first thing you see is the tempura display. It's lined up in a long row, and honestly it gets me excited ✨　There's fish tempura, sausage tempura, and vegetable ones too; it feels like Okinawa's “tempura culture” turned straight into a shelf. The interior is bright and clean, and I also like how casual it is, where you can eat quickly and leave quickly. In fact, customers never stopped coming, and seeing what looked like regulars buying with practiced ease, I thought, shops like this are strong~ 😌

My order this time was the “braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba” topped with fish tempura and sausage tempura. Rather than an Okinawa soba shop, the feeling of “a tempura shop where you can also eat soba” might fit better. It was served fairly quickly, and the moment I received it, it was the kind where you go, “Oh, it's soupy.” The visual volume was pretty impressive, and the sense of satisfaction comes first, as soon as it's set on the table 😂
Braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba　¥590
Braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba　¥590 + (fish, sausage tempura) ¥250

The soup is a combined broth with a light touch of pork bone. It has richness, but the overall impression is that the saltiness is a bit strong. Opinions may be divided, but on days when you've sweated or days when you want something strong, it seems like it would hit the spot for a lot of people 👍
Braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba　¥590 + (fish, sausage tempura) ¥250
Braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba　¥590

The noodles are medium-thick flat noodles with a loose wave. The texture is on the soft side. Personally, my honest feeling is that I'd be happy if they had just one more level of springiness~ 😅　However, the soupy broth clings to them well. I think people who like soft noodles can get hooked without worry.

And the tempura toppings. The fish tempura has a fluffy batter, and when you dip it in the soup a little, the batter gets moist and becomes a different kind of delicious. The sausage tempura has a junky feel that needs no explanation, and when something like this goes in, the “Uema-ness” comes out all at once 😋　Being able to add tempura bits for free is a quietly nice touch too.

Rating (9/15): Honestly, my overall verdict lands on “Yeah, it's ordinary.” There's no sharp edge like “Super moving!” or “One of a kind!”, but precisely because of that, there's a stability that makes it usable every day. It makes sense that there are so many customers, and I think the “convenient strength” of being able to enjoy tempura along with it is this shop's appeal 😊　Next time I'd like to go after other tempura and have fun from the tempura side 🍤✨

麺処 てぃあんだー.name: Mendokoro Tiandā
麺処 てぃあんだー.desc: A shop with house-made fresh noodles. Its specialty is the soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba with firm, flat noodles kneaded with fuchiba (mugwort), and the soki is served on a separate plate. The granular solid kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) is unusual too. The tables are old sewing machine stands.
t: This article was written with AI (Chat GPT 4o) and partially edited by me 😁
Okinawa soba tour 🚶‍♂️ I ate here in July 2024 😁　This time I visited “Mendokoro Tiandā” in Ameku, Naha City ✨.
Mendokoro Tiandā
Mendokoro Tiandā

When you enter the shop, wood-grain interior and a homey atmosphere spread out before you; it's a shop that somehow makes you feel nostalgic. Autograph boards displayed on the walls caught my eye, and I really felt that this is a shop loved by locals.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop (I don't know whose they are, but lots of celebrity autographs are posted on the walls)
Inside the shop (when I looked under the table I sat at, they were using an old sewing machine (^0^;) How nostalgic)
Menu

From the menu, I ordered the “soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba with fuchiba noodles” 😋. The words “house-made fresh noodles” on the entrance door caught my eye, raising my expectations. I waited excitedly, wondering what the combination of noodles kneaded with fuchiba (mugwort) and the uniquely Okinawan soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) would taste like.
Soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba (fuchiba noodles) ¥990

The soba that came out was beautiful from the look of it to begin with ✨. The greenish flat (thick?) fuchiba noodles float in a clear, light bonito broth soup, and ginger and mitsuba are gently placed on top. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), simmered until melt-in-your-mouth tender and served on a separate plate, really whet the appetite too 🍖.

First, a sip of the soup… Ooh! The bonito broth spreads slowly, a gentle taste that isn't heavy 😌. It's light, yet you can properly feel the umami, so it's a taste that makes you feel more relieved with every sip.
Soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba (fuchiba noodles) ¥990

And the flat (thick?) noodles! These are firm and really satisfying to eat 💪. The springiness you feel the moment you put them in your mouth is irresistible. It's a texture that reminds me a bit of the noodles at “Ishigufu,” and personally I like it a lot 😊.

The noodles kneaded with fuchiba (mugwort) have a faint grassy aroma too, and you can feel the Okinawan character. They're full of flavor, and I felt they add an accent to the taste of Okinawa soba, which can tend to be monotonous 🌿.

Next, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). They're served on a separate plate, a trick to keep their flavor from transferring to the soup. The soki itself is tender enough to fall apart in your mouth ✨ However, a little sinew remains, giving a balance with some chewiness / bite. You can eat them down to the bone, so it's a dish where you can fully enjoy traditional Okinawan cuisine 😋.

And this time the “kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori)” was a bit unique. Generally the liquid type is common, but here a granular solid type is provided 🧂. Both the look and the taste are a little different, and this was a little surprise. The heat isn't that strong, so I enjoyed changing up the flavor while dissolving it bit by bit into the soup 👍.

Rating (9/15): It was a reassuring Okinawa soba that tasted just plain delicious. The firmness of the flat noodles and the flavor of the fuchiba were especially memorable, but some people might feel the noodles are on the hard side. The soup and the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) also came together in an ordinary, well-balanced way 😌.

タイラ製麺所.name: Taira Seimenjo
タイラ製麺所.desc: A shop with house-made fresh noodles on Kokusai-dori, near Makishi Station on the monorail. The limited-quantity Taira soba is a bowl topped with thinly sliced skin-on pork belly like ramen chashu in a bonito broth soup. So popular it gets lots of Uber EATS orders.
t: I ate here in May 2024 😆　The other day I took part in the 13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally for the first time and completed it for the first time (34 shops, one round), and the stamp rally award ceremony was on Kokusai-dori, so I ate here before the ceremony 😄
Taira Seimenjo (it's on Kokusai-dori)
The menu posted on the wall
The menu posted on the wall

This time, from the menu, they said there was still some of the “Taira soba,” introduced as “limited quantity,” so I ordered it. It seems you can also change the noodles to mozuku noodles for an extra ¥50, but they said those were sold out, so I went with regular noodles 😄
After ordering, while I waited for a while, several Uber EATS orders came in, and delivery people came to pick them up several times. Given the great location on Kokusai-dori, they seem busy 😁
Taira soba　¥950
The Taira soba has arrived. First, the soup. It's a soup with the bonito broth coming through, and it's just plain delicious.
Taira soba　¥950
Next, I have the noodles. They're said to be house-made fresh noodles, a medium-thick straight type. They have a chewy texture, and these are fairly delicious too.
The skin-on pork belly is like ramen chashu: thinly sliced, tender, and falling apart 😋　This is delicious too.

Rating (9/15): Just plain delicious. It's on Kokusai-dori, close to Makishi Station on the monorail. How about trying it once between sightseeing? It seems to get lots of orders through Uber EATS too, so it looks popular 😄

識名そば.name: Shikina Soba
識名そば.desc: A popular shop near the World Heritage site Shikina-en. The selling points are a deep soup with a good balance of bonito and pork bone, and chewy house-made thin noodles. The extra-large braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba, limited to 3 servings on weekends, is first come, first served.
t: *I also had AI (Claude 3.5 sonnet) make this article, and I've edited and updated part of it myself lol

I'm Anji, an Okinawa soba blogger 😊 This time I went to “Shikina Soba” in Shikina, Naha City! On my Okinawa soba tour, I wonder how many shops this makes~ 🤔 I haven't counted, but I'm still nowhere near conquering them all, sa~ (Note: the AI is lying, so here's a correction. I've been to about 177 shops 😆). But I want to keep touring while enjoying each and every shop!

Well now, “Shikina Soba,” which I visited this time, has a conspicuous sign, so it was easy to find 😄 Looking at the exterior of the shop, it feels like a typical Okinawan shokudo, with a somehow nostalgic atmosphere 🏠
Shikina Soba
Shikina Soba

When you enter the shop, a meal ticket machine greets you. It's a shame it doesn't support cashless payment 👍 Looking at the menu, there's a wide variety of Okinawa soba! It's hard to decide. But this time I ordered the classic “soki soba” 😋

Actually I wanted to have the meal ticket machine's recommended top-left button, “extra-large braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba, limited to 3 servings on weekends,” but it was already sold out (^0^;) Too bad lol
The meal ticket machine installed near the shop entrance

The inside of the shop was bustling with customers. I went in right after opening, but the parking lot was full too, and I just barely got in (^0^;)　It feels like there are more tourists than locals. This raises my expectations~ 🔥
Menu (the words “house-made noodles” make me hopeful 😄)
Menu
Menu
Now, here comes the long-awaited “soki soba”! It looks delicious from the appearance alone 😍 Clear soup, plenty of green onions, and a big piece of soki on top.
Soki soba, large　¥850

As always, let's start by tasting the soup 🥄 Huh? Unexpected! I thought the bonito broth would hit hard at first, but I can clearly taste the pork bone flavor too. The balance of bonito and pork bone is exquisite, and if anything it's slightly bonito-based? The faint bonito flavor comes through, making it a deep taste. It's just plain delicious, but I don't think it has a standout characteristic~.
Soki soba, large　¥850

Next, let's go for the noodles! 🍜 They seem to use house-made noodles, a thin type. The chewy texture is nice~. They cling well to the soup too, and you can slurp them down smoothly~. I quite liked these! The house-made noodles are delicious 😋

And the toppings I was curious about, the bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki)~ 🍖 They look melt-in-your-mouth tender, but when I ate them they felt a bit dry. The sweet seasoning gives an Okinawan feel, but there are sinewy parts here and there, so the texture is uneven. Hmm, it might have been the best if they'd simmered them a bit more tender 😅

Looking at it overall, “Shikina Soba's” Okinawa soba is, I'd say, fairly delicious. There's no particularly surprising point, but it feels like an Okinawa soba with a stable taste. I think I understand why it's been loved by locals for a long time.
Now, let's do my usual Anji-style rating!
Rating (9.5/15): The noodles were the biggest selling point! The chewiness of the house-made noodles is irresistible for Okinawa soba lovers 😋

“Shikina Soba” is a little away from the tourist spots, but it was a lively shop bustling with tourists and locals. It's recommended for people sightseeing in Naha City or who want to get a little taste of the local atmosphere~.

However, it's a popular shop, so it may be crowded at lunchtime. When I went, I somehow just barely managed to park in the parking lot, but depending on the timing you might have to wait, so it might be good to visit with plenty of time to spare 😉

Finally, a little tip! Near “Shikina Soba” there's Shikina-en. It's a Ryukyu garden registered as a World Heritage site, a place where you can feel Okinawa's history and culture. It might be nice to take a little stroll after eating soba 🏯

Well, that's it for this Okinawa soba tour! Where should I go next~ 🤔 There must still be lots of delicious Okinawa soba shops in Okinawa. I'll keep bringing you the charm of Okinawa soba from here on!
Well then, see you next time! Have a good Okinawa soba life~ 🍜✨

沖縄そば 楚辺.name: Okinawa Soba Sobe
沖縄そば 楚辺.desc: A hugely popular shop with a striking old-folk-house-style building surrounded by trees. In the spacious interior lined with surfboards and celebrity autographs, the specialty is the “Three-Star Makanai Soba Set Meal” (with braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki)), limited to 30 servings a day.
t: I went to eat here in March 2025 😄 This time my Okinawa soba tour brings me to “Okinawa Soba Sobe” in Sobe, Naha City. The moment I arrived in front of the shop, my first impression was “Whoa, this place has a strong vibe.”
Okinawa Soba Sobe's parking lot
Okinawa Soba Sobe

An entrance like an old folk house surrounded by trees, and a sign full of character. Even though it's in town, the air feels a little more relaxed just there, and I totally get why people who come sightseeing get excited. In fact, the guide signs were conspicuous too, and even before going inside, there was a clear sense of “this must be a popular shop.”
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Inside, the spacious interior had surfboards on display and lots of celebrity autographs, and it was a very memorable space where Okinawan clutter mixed with touristy glamour 😊
Menu

What I had this time was the “Three-Star Makanai Soba Set Meal,” limited to 30 servings a day. The name alone has a bit of a special feel, and since it's topped with three kinds, braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), it's visually very satisfying. In fact, when it was brought out the bowl was quite luxurious, and I thought, “This is the kind that gets my hopes up.” The set meal comes with jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice), a small side dish, and even mozuku in vinegar, so I think it's a welcome lineup for tourists in terms of volume too. You can taste various aspects of Okinawa soba in one set meal, so it's an easy-to-understand set for first-timers.
Three-Star Makanai Soba Set Meal　¥1,550

First, the soup: among combined broths, it's a type where the pork bone's presence comes a bit to the front. It's just plain delicious, but it doesn't quite reach a personality that sticks strongly in your memory; that was my impression.
Three-Star Makanai Soba Set Meal　¥1,550
The noodles are thin, straight, and on the soft side. People who want to enjoy solid firmness and a wheaty feel might find them a bit lacking.

The toppings are braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), a lineup that gets you pretty excited just looking at the names. It had volume visually too, and a glamour worthy of the name “Three-Star.” But when I ate it, overall it leaned light, and I was bothered that each had a little sinewy texture remaining. If you're going to enjoy three kinds of meat, I'd have been happy if they were a bit more melt-in-your-mouth, or if the differences between each cut came through more clearly.

On the other hand, what was good were the small side dishes rounding out the set meal. The mozuku in vinegar was refreshing and felt great for resetting my palate. The bean sprout namul quietly did a good job too, and when small dishes like these are properly delicious, the satisfaction of the whole set meal goes up. The jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) was also on the light side, a balance that doesn't get in the way of the soba's taste. This might be why it's supported by tourists and a wide range of ages.
The table

However, I want to be honest here. The shop's atmosphere, its size, the building with a sense of history, the number of autographs, the number of tourists, even the special feel of the limited menu, all of it was there, so my expectations had gone up quite a bit. But when I actually finished eating, “just plain delicious” was my most honest impression 😅 It's not bad at all, and it's properly delicious. But it's also a fact that in Naha and Okinawa there are shops that grab you more with “the power of the soba itself.” That's exactly why I thought the reason so many people gather at this shop isn't just the taste, but must largely be its appeal including the strength of word of mouth, the shop's history, its location that's easy to visit while sightseeing, and that atmosphere.

Rating (9/15): I think it suits people who want to enjoy Okinawa soba leisurely in a spacious interior while feeling the Okinawan atmosphere on their trip. On the other hand, for people who “just want to be wowed by the taste of the soba alone,” I felt there's a chance it might be a bit of a letdown. It's worth going once including the atmosphere, but it wasn't a bowl that made me strongly feel I absolutely want to eat it again when I revisit. Still, actually going to a popular shop like this and confirming with my own tongue “so this is the type it is” is also part of the fun of an Okinawa soba tour 🌺
